title: The D-Score Snapshot Alignment Theorem: A Delay-Variance Budget for Asynchronous Biodiversity Indicators

claim_inventory.claim: Under normalized nonnegative effective weights in the stated local common-mode model, snapshot alignment efficiency has the exact weighted pairwise cosine-loss identity.
The modeled alignment efficiency lies in the unit interval.
For every modeled real angular frequency, alignment loss is at most angular frequency squared times weighted delay variance.
Within the declared frequency band and model assumptions, the weighted delay-variance budget is sufficient for the declared alignment floor.
Equal channel delays retain perfect modeled alignment.
Two equal-weight channels separated by a half cycle cancel the modeled common signal.
The captured adversarial suite reports 21 passed checks, zero failures, and no triggered preregistered failure condition for the stated analytic and synthetic model.

The cited literature documents temporal asynchrony and the need for explicit temporal harmonization in multi-source monitoring, while also cautioning that ecological asynchrony may be signal rather than error.
Channels share a locally common, linearly represented ecological mode after centering and scaling, with normalized nonnegative effective weights and known delays.
